newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel seals off Hebron to stifle unrest.
newsitem.headline: Israel seals off Hebron to stifle unrest.

text.p: Israel sealed off the West Bank town of Hebron on Friday to stifle unrest after a week of violence sparked by a Jewish poster depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig, the Israeli army and witnesses said.
At the confrontation line between Israeli- and Palestinian-run sectors of the city, some 50 Arab youths began throwing stones and bottles towards Israeli troops, witnesses said.
They said street activists from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's Fatah faction intervened, pushing back demonstrators in a bid to dampen the unrest.
"No clashes today!" shouted the activists to the jeers of demonstrators.
Witnesses said Israeli troops erected roadblocks around Hebron and turned back non-residents at entrances to the volatile city.
"Since the morning, the Israeli army is preventing the entrance of Palestinians who do not live in Hebron to (Palestinian-ruled) H1 area for security reasons," an army statement said.

Israeli bullets and Palestinian petrol bombs and stones have peppered the town since a Jewish woman ignited Arab anger by posting anti-Moslem placards depicting Mohammad as a pig stamping with one foot on the Koran.
Dozens of Palestinians have been wounded by Israeli troops firing rubber bullets and live ammunition in the confrontations.
Israel was bracing for more Hebron violence following weekly Moslem Friday prayers, security sources said.

Israeli Chief Rabbi Eliyahu Bakshi-Doron on Thursday met the Mufti of Hebron, the city's top Moslem cleric, to condemn the hate posters and to ask that he work to cool passions in the town holy to Moslem and Jew as the burial place of Abraham.
"Certainly, the entire Jewish people are disgusted by these deeds," Bakshi-Doron told Israel's army radio on Friday.
"I asked him to take all efforts not to fan the flames from a religious standpoint...this is a political dispute and certainly not one between Judaism and Islam."
Israeli leaders have condemned the hate poster.

Tatyana Suskin, a 26-year-old Jewish woman, was charged on Thursday with illegally posting the placards and with endangering life by stoning an Arab car on Saturday. The offences carry a 24-year maximum sentence.

But Palestinians have demanded that Israel remove the 400 Jewish settlers who remained in fortified enclaves under army guard in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs after Israel turned over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO self-rule in January.
"I want to make one thing clear: we will continue to live here and we will continue to build," Hebron Jewish settler Moshe Ben Zimra told army radio.
